text:
Community environment, 
psychological perceptions, and 
physical activity among older 
adults
Weiwei Liang1, HongzhiGuan2, HaiYan1 & Mingyang Hao1
The health of older adults is related to physical activity, and physical activity level (PAL) is associated 
with various factors such as community environment and psychological factors. Based on the above 
assumptions, this study constructs Structural Equation Modeling(SEM) to examined the relationship of 
psychological variables with older adults’ PAL. The study further combines observable variables such as 
socioeconomic attributes, travel characteristics, and objective community environment elements with 
latent variables to construct SEM-Logit model to examined the relationship between these factors 
and PAL. Our results showed that: (1) PAL was related to gender, age, living conditions, self-rated 
health, PA scope; (2) PAL was positively related to physical activity intention (PAI), and other perceived 
psychological variables had an indirect effect on PAL through PAI; (3) Older adults living in a walkable 
community are more likely to improve their PAL. Corresponding strategies were proposed from 
improving the community environment and guiding psychological perception.
Keywords Physical activity level, Older adults, Community environment, Perceived psychology, SEM, SEMLogit
The world population is aging rapidly. China has now entered a “moderate aging” society. Physical Activity 
(PA) is defined by Caspersen as any bodily movement produced by skeletal muscles that results in energy 
expenditure1. As age increases, the physiological functions of the older adult decline, chronic diseases increase, 
and physical activity decreases, which pose a threat to their physical and mental health. Appropriate physical 
activity has a positive effect on physical and mental health of the older adults2 and can effectively improve or 
maintain their health level3.
King and colleagues reported only 7.8% of older adults meeting the PA guidelines4. In U.S. and Swedish 
population studies employing objective activity measurement, fewer than 5% of adults over age 65 met physical 
activity recommendations5,6. Some studies have found that 72.4% of the older adults stated that they engaged 
in ≥5  h of physical activity each week7, 56.8% of the older adults were meeting the recommended physical

activity level8. There is little evidence about the overall physical activity level of the older adults in China. Nearly 
80% of the older adults in Qinhuai District, Nanjing, China did not reach the physical activity required to 
maintain health9. It can be seen that the total physical activity of the older adults is insufficient. How to make 
up for physical inactivity by increasing leisure-time physical activity (LTPA) has become a trending topic in 
the world10. In a survey conducted in 15 provinces of China in 2015, it was found that the participation rate of 
leisure-time physical activities of the older adults aged 65 and over was low (6.6%)11. A large number (67.3%) 
of the older adults in China are engaged in household activities (such as shopping, picking up and dropping 
off children, etc.)12. It is impossible to comprehensively evaluate the total physical activity level of the older 
adults only by specific types of physical activity. Indeed, it is the total amount of activity that is deemed to affect 
health13. Therefore, it is necessary to pay more attention to thetotal physical activity level of the older adults in 
China and what factors affect it.
In order to promote the physical activity (PA) of older adults, it is necessary to understand the related factors 
of PA. Previous researchers guided by the social ecological model to study that older adult individual having 
complex interrelationships among the intrapersonal, social and physical environment of a neighborhood7,14. 
The intrapersonal factors related to physical activity included gender, age, socioeconomic status, education

level, marital status, chronic diseases, obesity7
. The existing articles that focus on the relationship between 
the physical environment and total PA7,14,15 and specific areas of physical activities—recreational PA9,16–22,

recreational walking and transportation walking18,19,23–27 in older adults mainly involve in North-America, 
Europe, Australia28, with less studies conducted in Asian countries such as Japan, China. Although researches 
examining the relation among physical activity and neighborhood physical environment were carried out in 
many countries, empirical evidence of the influence of several aspects of the neighborhood built environment 
on physical activity among older adults is unclear and inconsistent7,28. This may be explained by variations 
in the environmental measures using objective measures, perceived measures or both, study populations18, or 
perception of the environment may vary with specific countries, regions and cultural backgrounds. There is a 
need for empirical research to examine the influence of community physical environment using objective and 
perceived measures on older adults to better understand the relation between community environment and 
older adult physical activity7.
The Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and the Health Belief Model (HBM) are two commonly used 
theoretical models to learn about beliefs influencing health-related behaviors, including physical activity29. 
In the TPB, attitudes, subjective norms and perceived behavioral control are three main constructs that could 
determine intentions to health-related behaviors30. In the HBM, perceived susceptibility and perceived severity, 
perceived benefits and barriers, self-efficacy are main components affecting health-related behaviors31. Social 
cognitive psychological factors such as perceived barriers and self-efficacy have also been proved to be related 
with physical activity. Carlson et al. found that walkability, social support and self-efficacy were associated with 
total MVPA min/week15. The factors influencing the physical activity of pregnant women included perception 
obstacles, action clues, exercise self-efficacy32. The linear regression model revealed a significant relationship of 
physical activity among (pre)frail older adults with descriptive norms, perceived barriers and attitudes29. This 
study found that intention did not correlate with the amount of PA undertaken33. Attitude and subjective norm 
were the strongest constructs associated with PA levels33. Intention is an important determinant of future PA 
behavior34. However, this study found that intention did not correlate with the amount of PA undertaken33. The 
association between intention and physical activity levels of older adults in China remains unknown. Previous

studies have investigated the physical activity of older adults based on TPB or HBM, but none of studies has used 
the integrated model of TPB and HBM to explore the association between these psychological variables and 
the physical activity intention or behavior of older adults in China. The integrated application of the TPB and 
HBM has been proved to more elucidate the beliefs related the health-related behavior, such as physical activity 
intention among (pre)frail older adults29, helmet use among electric bikers35. We believed that the integration 
of TPB and HBM would better determine the socio-cognitive associations with intention to undertake physical 
activity among older adults. In order to make up for this gap, this study aimed to determine the social-cognitive 
psychological factors based on TPB theory and HBM model associations with the intention and level to 
undertake physical activity (PA) among Chinese older adults.
Previous studies on physical activity levels mainly referred to the recommended standards of WHO7, using 
the weekly and daily minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA)14,15, weekly and daily minutes 
of light-to-vigorous physical activity (LVPA)14, meeting physical activity requirements (≥5 h per week)7 as the 
dependent variable. However, this study found that over 70% of the older adults almost never participate in 
moderate-intensity or above leisure physical activities9 and the older adults tend to engage in low-intensity 
physical activities in their daily lives36, which has been seldom considered in previous studies when quantifying 
the total physical activity level. Although the method of objectively measuring physical activity based on 
accelerometers14,15 has high accuracy, its testing cost is high, while the classical scale survey method has the 
advantages of saving time and convenience20,37. PASE scale is a classic scale to test the physical activity of the 
older adults, and its reliability and validity have been verified by the older adults in different countries37.
From the above analysis, it is considered necessary to consider several different levels of factors, including 
individual characteristics (demographic variables, health-related status, travel characteristics), subjective 
and objective community environment factors and social cognitive psychological factors of the older adults, 
especially the newly included variables such as whether the residential building had an elevator, community

walkability, and psychological perception variables. The broader study focused on several research questions7:
a. Are there significant differences in cognitive psychological factors among older adults with different physical 
activity levels?
b. What is the relationship between subjective and objective neighborhood physical environmental features 
and physical activity in older adults? Neighborhood walkability was not significantly associated with physical 
activity among older adults in Canada and United States7. So is the community walkability associated with 
total physical activity of Chinese seniors?
c. What is the relationship between cognitive psychological factors and physical activity level among older 
adults?
This study would contribute to a deeper understanding of the complex mechanisms underlying the older 
adults’ physical activity level and provide more comprehensive references for policy makers. This would be of 
great significance for improving the physical activity level of the older adults and enhancing/maintaining their 
health.

Methods and data
Sample
Survey region
China has now entered a moderately aging society. By 2023, the number of older people over 60 years old in 
China has reached 296 million, accounting for 21.1% of the total population in the country. At the end of 2023, 
the urbanization rate of China’s resident population was 66.16%, which means that two thirds of Chinese people 
live in urban areas. The resident population of megacities, super cities, Type I large cities, and Type II large 
cities accounts for about 54% of the total population in China. Based on the resident population size of urban 
areas, urbanization rate, and aging rate, three cities selected in this study included megacity (first tier cities in 
the world)—Beijing (B), super city (regional central city)—Qingdao (Q), and Type I Large City (coastal open 
city)—Yantai (Y) (see Table 1).
Respondents
People aged≥60 years old are called the older adults in China. Referring to the retirement age of Chinese 
residents, the subjects selected in this study must meet the following conditions: (1) they are under 60 years

old but have retired, or over 60 years old; (2) Living in the community for more than 6 months; (3) They can 
participate in physical activities independently.
The sampling procedure
This study is divided into two stages: pilot investigation and formal investigation.
In the pilot investigation stage: Firstly, we conducted face-to-face communication with some older 
respondents in the form of interviews to understand their needs for using community service facilities, as 
well as the common difficulties and perceived obstacles they face during their community daily trips. Through 
sorting and summarizing, we formed questionnaire survey questions; Then, several representative respondents 
were selected for a pilot investigation, and the questionnaire was tested and adjusted to ensure its validity and 
credibility.
Formal investigation stage: A questionnaire survey was conducted through a combination of online and 
offline methods from March 2023 to March 2024. This study first divides residential communities into two 
types based on unified standards: old and new communities. Communities built before 2000 are called old 
communities, while those built after 2000 are called new communities. The number of residential communities 
surveyed offline was based on a ratio of 1:2 between old and new communities. A total of 63 residential 
communities were selected, with a sample size of 5–20 per community. The sample for the online survey was 
randomly obtained from urban older people who were distributed questionnaires through channels such as WJX 
and WeChat.
The sampling size
Boomsma suggests: “When using maximum likelihood method to estimate structural equation models, the 
sample size should not be less than 20038. The sample size for structural equation modeling (SEM) needs to be 
5–10 times that of the observed variables39. This study obtained a total of 529 valid questionnaires, meeting the 
sample size requirements for structural equation modeling estimation methods in the field of behavior.
Measures
Demographics
On the basis of summarizing the previous literatures that affect the older adults’ physical activity level, 
demographic variables (age, gender, income, education level, residence or marital status, health status (number 
of chronic diseases, Body Mass Index (BMI), self-rated health status) were collected by survey. Living time in the

community and living conditions were also included in this study. The collected data also included the duration 
of a single trip, the frequency of daily trips, auxiliary tools, the PA scope (inside/outside the community) and the 
number of years of PA.
Psychosocial factor measures
The integration of Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and Health Belief Model (HBM) was validated, and it 
has been widely applied to explore the influence path of consumption behavior40,41, driving intention42, using 
intention35, beliefs of PA29, behavior intervention. Based on TPB and HBM, this study examined the relationship 
of perceptual psychological variables with older adults’ PAL.
In this study, subjective norm (SN) refers to the influence of society and people around (such as family 
members, sick relatives or friends, doctors, neighbors) on the older adults’ physical activities. Perceived benefits 
in HBM are similar to (positive) behavioral attitude (ATT) in TPB. Perceived Benefit (PBE) refers to the benefits

that the older individuals get from physical activities, such as relieving pain and getting spiritual satisfaction. 
Perceived behavioral control (PBC) refers to the cognition that an individual can complete a specific behavior 
according to the resources and opportunities he/she has mastered and the expected obstacles, as well as the 
accessibility and obstacles of available resources, which can be divided into personal factors, self-efficacy 
and external resources. In this study, PBC was defined as the influence of personal factors such as physical

health, income and free time on the older adults’ physical activities. External factors refer to the factors that the 
older adults think may obstruct their participation in physical activities, including weather conditions, venue 
conditions, activity facilities, convenience of traveling in community, etc.43, and thus introduced two variables: 
perceived barriers to facilities (PBAF) and perceived barriers in travel (PBAT). Perceived barriers to facilities 
(PBAF) refers to the obstacles perceived by the older adults when they use service facilities during PA. Perceived 
barriers in travel (PBAT) refer to the obstacles perceived by the older adults when they travel from home to the 
activity destination. Self-efficacy (SE) refers to the confidence to individual ability in the process of executing a 
certain behavior. Perceived severity (PSE) refers to an individual’s awareness of the severity of the consequences 
caused by diseases, such as shortened lifespan and inconvenience in daily life. Perceived susceptibility (PSU) 
refers to the probability that the older individuals think they are susceptible to chronic diseases.
The specific observation items of latent variables were shown in Appendix Table 1. Participants’ were asked 
about their level of agreement (1=strongly disagree, 2=somewhat disagree, 3=neutral (neither agree nor 
disagree), 4=somewhat agree, 5=strongly agree) inresponse to the all measured indicators.
Objective environment measures
The community physical environment factors associated with the older adults’ physical activities in the previous 
research are usually composed of density9,14,18,20,22, diversity9,18,20, design (including path quality19,20,22, road 
network linear density20, intersection density9,14,18,20,26, density14,20,26 or amounts of facilities15,18,19,22, greening 
rate9,26,plot ratio20), the distance to transit9,14,20,22,26, destination accessibility9,14,20,26 and distance to city center.
Walk Score was widely used in the measurement of walkability in European and American countries. Walk 
Score reflects the daily facilities configuration and the accessibility level of walking space within a certain range

around the starting point. About half of the older adults travel within 10 min (about 500 m). A single point Walk 
Score for each participant based on a 500-meter buffer around his/her home was created15. Walk Score measured 
by ArcGIS contains design and destination accessibility. Therefore, this study mainly considers several variables 
such as community type (old or new), whether there are elevators in residential buildings, walk score, population 
density from the objective measurement of community environment. Walk Score is normalized to 0-100. Walk 
score was divided into two categories: Car-dependent community with poor Walk Score<40 means that most 
of daily trips rely on a car, and walkable community with good Walk Score≥40 means that most daily trips rely 
on walking.
Perceived environment measures
Neighborhood Environment Walkability Scale (NEWS) is designed to subjectively measure residents’ perception 
of the walking environmental attributes of their local area, and it is widely used23,24. The questionnaire 
assessed the following environmental characteristics: aesthetics15,16,20–22,24–26, pedestrian traffic safety and 
crime safety7,20–22,24–26, residential density21,24,25, land use mix–diversity21,24,25, street connectivity21,24–26, ease 
of access to infrastructure7,20–22,24–26. These items instrument measured perceived attributes of neighborhood 
environment hypothesized to be related to physical activity44. Scholars have translated and revised the NEWS 
scale to make it suitable for local residents (such as Chinese seniors45, adults46 and urban community residents47
). This study will adopt the Chinese Walkable Environment Scale for urban community residents revised on the 
basis of Neighborhood Environment Walkability Scale-Abbreviated (NEWS-A)47, which subjectively measuring 
Chinese older adults’ perception of the community walking environmental attributes (see Appendix Table 2).
The scale includes the following aspects: ease of access (convenience) of supporting service facilities, road 
condition and aesthetics, traffic and safety. Participants were asked about their level of agreement (strongly 
disagree, somewhat disagree, neutral (neither agree nor disagree), somewhat agree, or strongly agree) in response

to the questions listed in the scale. Each item is graded from 1 to 5. The higher the score, the better the walking 
environment around the community48,49.
Physical activity level
Physical Activity Scale for Elderly (PASE) is an instrument that measures the level of physical activity for 
individuals aged 65 and older. It is considered that PASE scale can effectively and objectively measure the 
physical activity of the older adults in China37. The PASE is comprised of self-reported occupational, household 
and leisure items over a one-week period.
PASE scores are calculated from weights and frequency values for each of activities50. The total score of PASE 
is between 0 and 360. The higher the PASE score, the higher the physical activity level51. The PASE scores of the 
respondents were ranked from low to high, and the valid samples were equally divided into three groups50, that 
is, there were 176 people in the low physical activity level group, 177 people in the medium physical activity level 
group and 176 people in the high physical activity level group.
Hypotheses
Hypotheses about PAL
Based on the social ecological model, this study assumed that the physical activity level of the older adults 
would be related to socio-economic attributes (H1a), health status (H1b), living conditions (H2), activity-travel 
characteristics (H3), objective (H4a) and subjective (H4b) community environment. According to the TPB, 
intention was an important determinant of behavior, and perceived behavioral control can be a direct predictor

of behavior30. It was assumed that the older adults’ physical activity intention (PAI) was positively related to the 
physical activity level (PAL) (H5a). It was also assumed that there was a positive correlation between perceived 
behavioral control and older adults’ physical activity level (H5b). Therefore, the model framework of PAL among 
the older adults was shown in Fig. 1.
Hypotheses about PAI

Behavioral intention can be explained by three social-cognitive determinants - attitude, subjective norm, and 
perceived behavioral control30. When the more the older adults were influenced by family members, sick 
relatives/friends, doctors, neighbors, society and policies, the more they agreed with the statement of the physical 
benefits brought by participating in physical activities, the more they were supported by personal factors(such 
as income, health status, time) and the more confident they were able to participate in physical activities, the 
higher their intention to participate in physical activities would be; The older adults were afraid of the serious 
consequences of suffering from chronic diseases, and if the older adults encountered more obstacles in the 
process of undertaking physical activity and daily trips, their intention to engage in physical activity could be 
weaken. the following hypotheses H6a~H6g are proposed:
Subjective norm (H6a), activity attitude/perceived benefits (H6b), perceived behavioral control (H6c), selfefficacy (H6d), perceived susceptibility (H6e), perceived barriers to facilities (H6f), perceived barriers in travel 
(H6g), and perceived severity (H6h) are significantly associated with the older adults’ physical activity intention 
(PAI).
Bamberg et al. found that subjective norm had positively effect on attitude52, and Cai Yunhao et al. found that 
subjective norm have a positive and significant impact on the driving attitude of the older adults42. It was found 
that perceptual behavior control had a positive effect on attitude53, while Perceptual barriers was negatively 
associated with attitude42,54. Therefore, the following hypotheses are proposed:
Subjective norm (H7a), perceived behavioral control (H7b), perceived susceptibility (H7c), perceived 
severity (H7d) are positively related to the older adults’ attitude towards PA. Perceived barriers to facilities (H7e), 
perceived barriers in travel (H7f) are negatively related to the older adults’ attitude towards PA. There was a 
significant correlation between SN and PBC, PBAF, PBAT, and PBAF is correlated with PBAT (H7g).
Through the warning of sick older people around them, listening to the advice of doctors and other

professionals, the older adults would realize that they were prone to chronic diseases and the serious consequences 
if they get sick. The people who were prone to suffering from chronic diseases would be more aware of the 
serious consequences they bring to individuals and families. Therefore, the following hypotheses are proposed:
H8a Subjective Norm is associated with Perceived Susceptibility;
H8b Perceived Susceptibility is associated with Perceived Severity;
H8c Subjective Norm is associated with Perceived Severity;
The greater the support of the people around them, society and policies, the more they agreed with the statement 
that participation in physical activities brought physical benefits, the higher the support of personal factors 
(economy, time, health, etc.), the more they thought that they were prone to suffering from chronic diseases and 
the more they were afraid of the serious consequences caused by illness, the more confident they would be able

to participate in activities. If the older adults encounter more obstacles in physical activity and daily trips, their 
perception of self-efficacy would weaken. From this, we put forward the following assumptions:
Subjective norm (H9a), attitude (H9b), perceived behavioral control (H9c), perceived susceptibility (H9d), 
perceived severity (H9e), perceived barriers to facilities (H9f) and perceived barriers to travel (H9g) are 
associated with self-efficacy.
Method
The research includes the analysis process of hypothesis-modeling-testing. Statistical analysis was calculated 
using SPSS 19.0. The Goodman and Kruskal tau-y coefficient was used to measure the asymmetric correlation 
between two categorical variables, which was also applicable to measuring the correlation between a categorical 
variable and an ordinal variable. The asymmetric correlation between two ordinal variables was measured 
using the dy coefficient. The difference of physical activity level among the old people with different attributes 
was tested by Pearson Chi-Square, and the difference of psychological perception among the older adults with

different physical activity levels was analyzed by one-way ANOVA. The test level is α=0.05.
The SEM model constructed using Amos 17.0 was used to examined the relationship of latent variables 
including perception of community environment and cognitive psychological factors with PAI and PAL 
among older adults. On this basis, the observable variables such as demographic variables, health status, travel 
characteristics and objective community environmental factors such as Walk Score, population density, were 
further combined with the latent variables in the SEM model, and the relationship between these variables and 
physical activity level was examined by using SEM-Logit model.
Results
Descriptive statistics
Demographic characteristics
Table 2 summarizes the main population characteristics of the effective sample. An age mean of the respondents 
was 66 years old, and the oldest was 90 years old. Nearly 70% of the respondents had junior high school education. 
Nearly 70% of the respondents had no elevators in their residential buildings. About 35% of the older adults said 
that they have lived in the community for more than 20 years. 70% of them suffer from one or more chronic 
diseases. Less than 20% of the older adults rated their physical health as good.
Difference of PAL among different groups of older adults
There are statistical differences in the PAL of the older adults with different gender, age groups, income, education 
level, occupation, living conditions, living time in the community, suffering from chronic diseases (0, ≥1), selfrated health status, auxiliary tools (required/not required), maximum walking distance per trip, travel time, 
travel frequency, go outside the community (yes/no), physical activity time, work (with/without) and Walk Score 
(P<0.05) (see Table 3).
Psychological factors and physical activity level
One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) was used to compare the effect of perceived psychological variables 
on of physical activity level. Subjective norm, self-efficacy, perceived susceptibility, perceived benefit, perceived 
severity and physical activity intention of the older adults with different levels of physical activity were statistically 
significant (P<0.05), but there were no significant differences in perceived behavior control, perceived barriers 
to facilities, perceived barriers in travel and community walking environment perception with PAL of older

adults (P>0.05), as shown in Table 4.

Model modification

Model result analysis
As can be seen from the results of path analysis,
(1) Subjective norm (β=0.32), perceived benefits/attitudes (β=0.27), perceived behavioral control (β=0.13) 
and self-efficacy (β=0.27) had significant positive effects on the older adults’ physical activity intention. 
Perceived severity (β=- 0.12) and perceived barriers in travel (β=- 0.10) had significant negative effects on 
the older adults’ physical activity intention.

SEM-Logit model
Quantitative perceptual psychological variables were obtained through the results of the SEM model mentioned 
above. Combining with socio-economic attributes, living conditions, health status, travel characteristics and

objective community environment measurements, SEM-logit model was constructed to analyze the relationship 
between these independent variables and physical activity level  (PAL). Odd ratio (OR) and 95% confidence 
intervals [95% CIs] were used to evaluate the association between the dependent variable, physical activity level, 
and independent variables7.
Based on the estimation results of the model parameters (see Table 8), it can be seen that gender, age, selfrated health status, living conditions, with/without elevator, PA scope, PA time, Walk Score, perceived road 
condition (PRC) and physical activity intention (PAI) had significant effects on the older adults’ physical activity 
level.
Relation between demographic variables and physical activity level (PAL)
Socio-demographic and health related variables were also associated with the older adults’  physical activity 
level (PAL), and in the expected direction7. Significant associations were observed for gender, such that male 
respondents (vs. female: OR [95% CIs]=0.44 [0.31–0.62]; p<0.000) were less likely to improve the physical 
activity level. The probability that the PAL of older men increasing one unit was 0.44 times that of older women. 
Significant associations were observed for age, such that respondents ages 60–64 years (vs. ≥75 year olds: OR 
[95%CIs]=11.69 [6.05–2.61]; p<0.000), were more likely to improve the physical activity level. The probability

Discussion and conclusion
Discussion
This study constructed an integrated model of TPB&HBM, and used exploratory factor analysis (EFA) to

determine the socio-cognitive associations with intention (and level) to undertake physical activity among 
community dwelling Chinese older adults. The integrated model has good reliability and validity, so the 
TPB&HBM integration model can effectively explain the older adults’ physical activity. It was found that the 
older adults’ intention to undertake physical activity was positively correlated with their physical activity level 
in our study, which highlights the good translation of behavioral intention into behavior33. Different from our 
findings, prior research among (pre)frail older adults in China29 and Chinese female college students with 
vulnerable conditions56, intention was not associated with physical activity29. The weakened intention-behavior 
relationship might be because vulnerable or frail individuals encountered physical difficulties in exerting their 
intentions29. Another study among community dwelling British South Asian adults aged 60 and over33also 
failed found the association. It remains to be determined if intention is a significant determinant of behavior for 
this population group in different countries33. Nonetheless, this study still provides an important contribution 
to our understanding of the relationship between Chinese older adults’ intention and level of undertaking 
physicalactivity33. Our study also found that perceived behavioral control (PBC) was not associated with physical 
activity level, although PBC associated with physical activity intention. This indicates that perceived behavioral 
control (PBC) play distinct roles in the different stages of physical activity among Chinese older adults29.

We found that the perceived severity (PSE) was negatively correlated with the older adults’  physical activity 
intention. Different from our finding, the research on the (pre)frail older adults found that the perceived physical 
threat was positively related to the intention of physical activity29. We also found that perceived barriers in travel 
(PBAT) was negatively correlated with the older adults’ physical activity intention. Individuals’ perception of 
risks of negative consequences and barriers encountered in the process of daily trips may prompt the older adults 
to reduce their opportunities and initiative to participate in physical activities in order to reduce risks or barriers. 
In line with prior research33, attitude and subjective norm were related to intention to undertake PA.
In this study, the SEM-logit model was further constructed to explore the relationship between individual 
socio-economic attributes, psychological perception variables based on TPB and HBM, objective and subjective 
community environment characteristics and older adults’ physical activity level. The following findings were 
mainly discussed around social-economic characteristics and subjective and objective community environment.

The study found that physical activity level among Chinese older adults was related to gender, age, living 
conditions, self-rated health, going outside the community. Older women had a higher level of physical activity. 
With the increase of age, the possibility of improving the older adults’ physical activity level were less likely. The 
possible explanation for this phenomenon is that with the increase of age, the physiological functions of the 
older adults continue to decline and the activity ability further declines21. The study found that good health had 
a positive role in promoting the leisure physical activities of the older adults21, it was found that the physical 
activity level of the older adults who self-rated health as good was higher. This phenomenon may be related to 
the fact that older adults with chronic diseases were often constrained by their physical conditions and it was 
difficult to maintain regular physical activities for them21. One important finding was that the older adults with 
elevators in their residential buildings have a high level of physical activity. From this, we initially think that the 
installation of elevators in residential buildings may be of great significance to improve the physical activity level 
of the Chinese urban older adults.
We also found that half of the older adults participate in physical activities within 500 m from home. Based 
on the community walking score of the 500-meter buffer around the home, it was found that the older adults 
living in walkable communities had a higher level of physical activity. Different from our findings, neighborhood 
walkability was not significantly associated with meeting physical activity requirements7. Likewise, older people 
who can go outside the community have a higher level of physical activity. In line with prior research57, we also 
found that there was no significant correlation between population density, intersection density and the older 
adults’ physical activity level, which may be related to the dense community population and road network and 
the large number of intersections in China. In this study, it was found that the increase of population density was 
helpful for the older adults to participate in leisure physical activities, and the intersection density and greening 
rate had negative effects on the physical activities of the older adults9.
For the subjective community walking environmental factors, we found that the perceived road conditions 
had a significant negative impact on the older adults’ physical activity level. In line with prior research7,57, the

convenience of supporting living facilities, traffic conditions, aesthetics and perceived public safety were not 
related to the older adults’ physical activity level, which may be related to the fact that the older adults at different 
physical activity levels had no obvious differences in perceived community environmental factors. Perceived 
neighborhood environment was related with walking for specific purposes23,58, it is found that aesthetics, street 
connectivity and accessibility are the main built environment factors that affect the leisure walking level of the 
older adults59–61, neighborhood aesthetics are associated with adults’ recreational walking24. Built environmental 
factors (e.g., sidewalks, crosswalks, crossing lights, benches, lighting) are important predictors of physical 
activity, especially for older adults whose daily activities often contract to more immediate surroundings (e.g., 
home environment, neighborhood)7.
Social support and self-efficacy were associated with physical activity15. According to the research results 
from SEM, we found that social cognitive psychological variables based on TPB and HBM models indirectly 
were related to physical activity level (PAL) through physical activity intention (PAI). Overall, perceived barriers 
to facilities (PBAF) (e.g., exercise venue, benches, public toilet), perceived barriers in travel (PBAT) (e.g., 
disorderly parked vehicles, steps) and perceived road condition (PRC) (e.g., lighting, smoothness of sidewalks 
and crosswalks, greening rate, cleanliness) all had negative effects on the older adults’  physical activity level 
(PAL). Physical activity intention (PAI) and subjective norm (SN) were the strongest constructs positively 
associated with the older adults’ physical activity level (PAL).
Conclusions
Based on the integrated model of TPB and HBM, this study explored the relationship between psychological 
variables and older adults’ physical activity intention and level. The integration model has been proved to be 
effective and reliable. Based on SEM-logit model, this study comprehensively considered comprehensively 
considers the subjective and objective community environment, individual socio-economic attributes and 
social cognitive psychological variables at different levels, and determined the relationship between these factors 
and the older adults’ physical activity level. This would contribute to understanding the complex influencing 
mechanism underlying the physical activity level among the older adults.
Practical implications

This study found that older adults’ physical activity level was closely related to multiple levels of factors, 
including socioeconomic attributes, living conditions, health status, activity travel characteristics, subjective and 
objective community environmental factors, and social cognitive psychological factors based on TPB and HBM, 
which recognizes the complexity of older adults’ physical activity. Older adults living in a walkable community 
are more likely to improve their physical activity level. A walkable community environment with supportive 
infrastructure, such as flat and clean roads, various service facilities, can play an enabling role in mobility and

physical activity in older adults. The psychological perception of physical activity among the older adults, such 
as perceived benefits/attitudes, self-efficacy, perceived severity, and perceived barriers in travel, was indirectly 
related to their physical activity level through their intention to undertake physical activity. The findings can 
also provide reference opinions for urban planners and health managers. Therefore, relevant measurements 
or implementing policies proposed from the aspects of transforming the community travel environment and 
guiding social cognitive psychology of older adults, which can provide reference for maintaining or improving 
their physical activity level and health.
In China, efforts are being made to comprehensively promote the renovation of old urban communities, 
with a focus on renovating those built before the end of 2000. Based on the findings in this study, the following 
measures have been proposed in terms of community hardware facilities: (1) Residential buildings in old 
communities would be equipped with elevators to increase opportunities for outdoor activities for older adults; 
(2) Based on the usage needs of older adults for community service facilities (CSF) such as leisure chairs, public 
toilets,and activity areas, improve the configuration of CSF and reduce the perception barriers to facilities 
(PBAF) among older adults; (3) By improving the community walking environment, such as checking ramps 
and road conditions, the perceived barriers in travel would be reduced; and (4) creating a walkable community 
enables the older adults to reach the destinations of various activities within a suitable walking distance, which

increases the opportunities of travel for the older adults and helps to improve their physical activity level.
On the individual psychological level, experts who are familiar with psychology, kinematics, medicine and 
other fields help to improve the older adults’ awareness of health beliefs, make the older adults participate in 
physical activities suitable for themselves, and meet the needs of the older adults for disease prevention and 
treatment, strengthen body, enjoy life, social interaction, and so on.
Limitations
Some limitations should be mentioned in our study. First, all the participants were randomly surveyed in large 
cities in China, which precluded the generalizability to other populations, especially those from urban areas, 
especially those from small cities, and rural areas. Considering the tendency of population’s aging and the 
extension of life expectancy, Further studies recruiting a wider range of older adults with larger sample sizes are 
recommended. In China, there are many older adults living in old communities, and future research can focus 
on old communities. In addition, the measurement of the older adults’ physical activity level in this study was 
based on the self-reported PASE scale, and the older adults may have some deviations in recalling their activities 
in the past week. The data reflecting physical activity can be obtained by objective measurement method such 
as motion sensors, which can reflect the real level of physical activity and increase the scientific and reasonable 
research results. In addition, this study is limited by the cross-sectional design, and longitudinal research can be 
carried out in the future.
